This work delves into a particular type of nilpotent algebra by exploring how its multiplicative structure interacts with its vector space geometry. To this end, a specific class of geometrically congruent algebras is introduced, characterized by a shared invariant known as the nilpotency index. A comprehensive description of this special class has been established for algebras of a particular dimension, alongside established connections with other special algebraic systems. Furthermore, a significant problem related to the existence of such cones has been successfully resolved in cases of low nilpotency indices.

Research focuses on the impact of Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) on the development of active galactic nuclei and their jets, particularly at high redshift levels of $z \ge 3$. This study utilizes self-similar magnetohydrodynamic simulations to examine the development of powerful radio jets emitted from supermassive black holes into their surrounding environments of low-density and predominantly turbulent nature. By applying a range of radiative feedback mechanisms, we here solely focus at the impact of Compton-scattering off the CMB as a possibly limiting factor which can prevent jets from achieving long distances. It's found from our simulations the CMB does not have a substantial influence on jet morphology or propagation over vast distances of hundreds of parsecs to the megaparsecs. Instead what we here find is that self-adjusting jet power provides for very different outcomes from pre-heated jets with fixed power, which prior studies have through a simple one-zone approach previously modeled and found to be either limited by the inverse Compton process at the thermal stage or able to persist for vast distances. It's moreover discovered that transverse magnetic fields do not have a substantial impact on jet morphology regardless of CMB conditions and furthermore that jets with pre-heating display strong afterglow levels of significant relevance to very early radio astronomy observations. In contrast, jets not pre-heated display very little afterglow, which is of particular relevance in understanding the development of supermassive black holes seeds in the early universe.

A comprehensive set of non-dissipative Lagrangians for classical gravity is constructed, including all possible coupling terms between the metric and curvature tensors. Utilizing the equivalence principle and analysis of conservation laws, it's demonstrated that the derived set is exhaustive. The method involves first establishing that dissipation is incompatible with a principle of stationary action. Next, all coupling terms between the metric and the curvature tensor are determined, and it's shown that these terms can be expressed through three independent structures. Finally, a classification of energy-momentum tensors capable of generating a gravitational field is provided.

The accuracy of neural networks is compromised when images are distorted or deformed. Researchers have attempted to counter this challenge by using approaches like using scaled datasets, which is inefficient and cumbersome to implement. We propose a new approach to improve generalization by applying a volume realignment pre-processing step before training, without the need for additional data. We combine strategies from scaling and data augmentation to explore various brain scan shapes and improve model performance. We evaluate our approach on our collected dataset and two public evaluation platforms, comparing results with and without volume realignment, and finding better performance consistently across different models and evaluations. We also propose an efficient, convolutional network-based learning module that leverages the proposed pre-processing step.

Our analysis of photometric data from AAVSO reveals an intriguing double-degenerate binary star system, SDSS J082239.54+304857.19, characterized by its 40.5-minute eclipsing cycle. The light fluctuations we observed reveal a notable long-term trend spanning from 2007 to 2020, marked by a progressive decline in amplitude and a gradually decreasing trend in period amounting to -2.7s over 2020 years. The observed variations we discovered in the star's properties could be a direct manifestation of mass transfer occurring within the binary star system.

Recent advancements in image processing and signal analysis have utilized Global Average Pooling (GAP) effectively, yet its underlying mechanics remain poorly understood. This paper provides a clearer insight into GAP's behavior, showcasing that it corresponds to a 1-D optimal transport problem with a straightforward solution. We demonstrate that this optimal transport problem can be resolved by employing the optimal scoring function in a score-based deep learning model, even in the most basic case of 1-D data. Furthermore, this perspective offers valuable insights into incorporating GAP into various complex data types and incorporating score-based deep learning modules to develop new GAP-based layers, ultimately leveraging the GAP scoring function as a powerful,可微分 metric for assessing representation quality and guiding network refinement.

The relationship between the host galaxy of an active galactic nucleus (AGN) and its orientation has been the subject of ongoing research for the past two decades. Our new analysis of SDSS data reveals distinct differences in AGN subtypes. Type 1 AGNs are mostly found in randomly oriented galaxies, whereas type 2 AGNs exhibit a stronger tendency for aligned subcomponents. Furthermore, we discovered that near-infrared luminosity impacts AGN orientation distribution, with brighter galaxies displaying an increased alignment prevalence. Notably, we observed a higher alignment prevalence among both high-luminosity Type 1 and low-luminosity Type 2 near-infrared galaxies. These distinctions suggest varying nuclear activity levels and orientation selection biases among the types. We also analyzed the stellar mass (M*) influence, discovering a weak positive correlation between M* and alignment prevalence. Both luminosity and M* trends hint at an enhanced gas and star activity in early-stage galaxies that decreases with time.

This paper investigates complete flat rotation surfaces with pointwise 1-type Gauss maps in E4. It is established that such surfaces have a certain type of rotation curve. Furthermore, complete directly rotated surfaces with 1-type Gauss maps are classified. Additionally, the classification of complete centrally rotated surfaces with 1-type Gauss maps is provided.

Deep neural network-based depth assessment is a well-established area of study. In contrast, scene segmentation based on detailed high-level classifications has not as much attention. Recent research suggests that depth assessment algorithms can be utilized to improve scene segmentation algorithms. However, there has not been any thorough investigation into whether these improvements stem from the excellent self-supervised learning capabilities of depth assessment algorithms. Our research focuses on this question. Using these models for their implicit self-supervision would be beneficial as they don't require labor-intensive annotated data like classification algorithms do. Our analysis revealed that when combining depth assessment and classification algorithms with a pre-existing dataset (Cityscapes), the improvements seen were slightly negative when pressure on pixel-level accuracy was relaxed by removing the depth assumption. Therefore, it was concluded that the enhanced performance from using depth assessment algorithms was not necessarily indicative of superior pre-training capabilities.

High-quality signposts play a crucial role in guiding the model to create new story segments, which in turn improves the overall model performance and prevents it from copying existing content extensively. As the story progresses, signoff frequency dynamically adjusts, reflecting the evolving narrative direction and direction changes. These frequency patterns are directly linked to the story's underlying structure and context, providing valuable insights into its development and progression.

The ATLAS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) has conducted detailed studies on the properties of beauty mesons. Specifically, the group focused on evaluating the precise measurement of rare decay occurrences and CP violation within these mesons. Additionally, the group presented an overview of related studies involving beauty meson pairs.

On a Cayley tree, we analyze periodic Ising models with both one-dimensional and two-dimensional structures. Focusing on novel weakly periodic configurations, we examine the phase transition phenomenon by determining the set of magnetic fields and interaction parameters for which the model admits a unique Gibbs measure on the tree. For specific types of weakly periodic configurations, we prove the existence of non-empty regions in the parameter space where only one weakly periodic configuration exists, resulting in a unique Gibbs measure. To our knowledge, this is the first time such a characterization has been achieved on a Cayley tree.

A new type of hyperbolic cauchy issues with space dependent, sublogarithmic small coefficients is explored. A comprehensive theory exists for a specific subset of these issues, defined by their coefficient structure and bounded by a sublogarithmic threshold. It's proven that any issue in this category is equivalent to one where the coefficients reduce to zero as duration increases, all while maintaining the same time scale. To achieve this equivalence, a novel approach is introduced, involving the factorization of pseudodifferential operators and a novel class of function spaces.

The process of extracting individual words from written Japanese text is known as term segmentation. This task has been successfully accomplished using supervised machine learning approaches such as Maximum Entropy, Conditional Random Fields, and neural networks. However, these methods rely on short-term memory for processing, which according to research in human neuroscience is insufficient for certain tasks. This paper introduces an advanced framework called Short-Term Memory and Extended Short-Term Memory networks, designed to remember and correlate information over extended periods. These networks have been applied to the challenging task of Japanese term segmentation and have achieved remarkable results, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods by over 3% in unbalanced evaluation and demonstrating improved generalizability without requiring extensive training data.

Programmers frequently seek assistance on Stack Overflow (SO) for problems they encounter, 
but the platform's requirement for questions to have at least one accepted answer means 
developers may need to search outside the community for help. A significant portion of 
programmers discover solutions through the code they write on platforms like GitHub, 
so we investigate the connection between successful Stack Overflow questions and external resources found on GitHub or other development-related sites. 
We analyze a large dataset of GitHub-indexed SO questions, revealing that the external resources programers share are often not the best solution, 
but rather a starting point for further development. This study provides insights into programers' behavior and the potential benefits of incorporating GitHub into SO's evaluation criteria.

Recent studies found that the relationship between a galaxy's luminosity and its surrounding halo mass breaks down below a certain luminosity threshold, which challenges the ability of galaxy formation models to account for this pattern. It has been suggested that the breakdown of this relationship marks a transition from radiation-dominated to matter-dominated processes, but the physical basis for this assumption remains unclear. Using an N-body simulation, we examined whether a distinct change in halo mass occurs at this luminosity threshold. Our study found that the masses of halo minispheroids, with a radius of approximately 1.5 kiloparsecs, do not significantly change below the critical luminosity threshold. This indicates that variation in halo mass cannot solely explain the broken galaxy mass-halo relation and likely other physical factors are responsible. We explored the mass assembly history, gravitational potential, and mass distribution of these minispheroids but were unable to identify characteristics correlated with the galaxy mass. Therefore, additional physical processes, likely driven by radiation, are probably at the heart of the broken galaxy mass-halo relation.

Effective climate change communication is crucial due to the significant influence of daily weather forecasts on human behavior. Although a variety of climate information exists, the tools for disseminating it are not uniformly available to various user groups. Our study presents a large-scale climate information repository that facilitates the customization of a climate information website tailored to different user requirements. This customizable platform enables the seamless integration of an underlying climate data set with front-end technologies such as Shiny and D3.js, thereby allowing for impactful climate change communication. We discuss the challenges encountered during the deployment of our climate repository and highlight the advantages of using a scalable information repository to enhance public climate awareness.

Domain-specific pretraining is generally required for effective Note Learning, but preprocessing medical text is challenging due to extensive annotations found in medical clinical notes and a high level of language complexity. We are examining the concept of domain generalization for the task of extracting sign events in medical notes, focusing on creating a robust NLP model that can operate without prior medical pretraining. Our method involves experimenting with different data enhancement methods to generate synthetic clinical notes for pretraining and a technique called REgularized Ensemble, which combines model training and data generation to develop a prior distribution for the task. Our findings are presented within the clinical NLP competition framework.

Profound RL is a two-component autonomous system that integrates the benefits of intrinsic autonomy and extrinsic autonomy. Intrinsic autonomy is responsible for decision-making by determining the most suitable driving strategy under various conditions, whereas extrinsic autonomy executes the decision by generating control signals to achieve the intended outcome, whether the decision was made by the intrinsic module or not. This paper details the design of Profound RL's architectural framework and demonstrates its effectiveness in navigating a variety of challenging scenarios.

Categorizing data efficiently across various domains poses a significant challenge. A common solution lies in class-specific CNNs, yet they come with the burden of a substantial number of parameters, leading to excessive memory requirements and slow processing speeds. Our proposed approach successfully mitigates these drawbacks by employing a spiking CNN composed ofRRUs, which leverages a backpropagation-free learning algorithm to optimize the timing of individual neurons. This innovative structure incorporates an entropy-driven categorical selector that pinpoint'specific classes and streamlines the CNN's operations by eliminating unnecessary computations. As a direct consequence, our method as a low-bandwidth, energy-efficient solution outperforms traditional methods, delivering enhanced performance speedup and reduced power consumption on sequential hardware platforms.

The thermal properties of spin-aligned strange quark matter under high-temperature and strong-magnetic-field conditions are investigated. According to the MIT bag model, this research examines the feasibility of spin-aligned strange quark stars存在 under these conditions. An analytical equation of state derived from the free-quark model, taking into account the quark's spin alignment in a magnetic field, enables the construction of the mass-radius relationship for these stars. Findings indicate that both the maximum mass and radius of these stars decrease when the magnetic field strength increases. At temperatures as high as $10^{11}$ K, the calculated radii of these stars fall within the observed radius range of neutron stars, raising the possibility of the existence of spin-aligned strange quark stars in this temperature range.

Traditional distributed computing projects like SETI@home and Google Photoshave achieved success in enhancing system performance through volunteer-basedworkloads. However, they typically rely on pre-installed client software and acentralized model that assigns tasks directly. In contrast, we've developed an innovative approach that leverages natural interactions between browsers and websites to execute performance-intensive tasks. Specifically, our framework utilizes advanced techniques like JavaScript compilation, browser extensions, and sponsored content to create workloads that optimize the bandwidth between browsers and server-side services. Furthermore, these services are designed using parallel execution and online learning principles to achieve functionalities such as real-time load balancing and resource management. Since our framework naturally integrates with browsers and requires no special installation, it provides an optimal solution for optimizing browser-based performance with minimal overhead.

The solution space characterization problem for matricial nonlinear eigenproblems involves finding characteristically compact operator sequences with matrix functions as their respective generators. Traditional approaches to this problem rely on the use of vector valued rational functions and matrix valued functional models, which have specific advantages but are limited by their specific requirements. However, a new approach developed in this characterization utilizes an alternative method involving the minimal rational interpolation theory that overcomes these limitations and provides a general solution to the characterization problem. This novel approach allows for the dynamic estimation of the nonlinear eigenproblems by applying a sequence of rational functions that converge to the solution space characterization and can be computed using data from the nonlinear eigenproblems as their R-matrix values. Furthermore, this new method provides an alternative approach to solving the solution space characterization problem and may find applications in conjunction with the R-matrix theory.

The focus of this research is on the concept of $\beta$-transformation, specifically $\beta$-transitions which serve as key building blocks in unit intervals with a specified gap and serve to distinguish a class of $\beta$-transitions related to fully intermediate $\beta$-transitions. A systematic approach has been developed for analyzing greedy $\beta$-transitions resulting from transferring the orbit of $0$ across some or all gaps in the transformation. This method enables the identification of fully intermediate $\beta$-transitions in various scenarios, and it has significant implications, particularly in the areas of number theory and probability theory where $\beta$-transformation is widely applied.

We analyze a lattice QCD-like theory with $q$ quark flavors interacting with $N_{cf}$ colors through an $SO(N_{cf})$ gauge interaction, computing the static quark-antiquark potential and dressing phase within the dilute instanton gas approximation. We find disruption of chiral symmetry due to a $q/N_{cf}$ dependence causing a phase transition within the flavor space, supported by the presence of a gauge theory anomaly. Furthermore, to address the issue of unbroken center symmetry, we introduce a new quark mass term, the "walking mass," which is flavor blind and does not mix chiral symmetries. This allows for a proper lattice simulation with unbroken center symmetry, facilitating the observation of confinement and disruption of chiral symmetry simultaneously, provided the fondly present instantons exist.

The use of feature importance in machine learning models has long been essential, yet its limitations have prompted a search for more sophisticated explanation methods, such as partial dependence plots, SHAP, and LIME. Despite their efforts, these techniques often fall short in fully disentangling feature effects. This study introduces a novel approach called assignment curves to provide clear and accurate model interpretations by separating the influence of individual features on predicted outcomes. Drawing on fundamental tree and forest working principles, this new technique calculates how each feature assigns training data points and utilizes this information to construct an assignment curve. Unlike traditional explanation methods, this approach leverages information about in-sample data without the need for out-of-sample re-sampling. Additionally, it offers a novel way to evaluate feature interaction by observing a forest model's composition and is applicable to any random forest structure without restriction. Furthermore, this method can be easily adapted to use test data or extended to handle classification and regression models.

Federated learning allows training models across multiple devices without sharing sensitive data. However, its implementation faces significant performance challenges. To overcome this, a solution called Flatee is proposed, which leverages hardware solutions like Intel SGX to secure the model parameters and reduce data transmission size by encryption-based consensus reaching. The system learns collaboratively across isolated environments without exposure to sensitive data, supported by a novel protocol that supports model updates, data transmission, and security within a network. The Flatee framework also automatically manages the verification process and ensures the integrity of model updates using a technique called Remote Attestation. The framework's feasibility and effectiveness are demonstrated through open-source realization and empirical evaluation, which indicates improved data privacy and efficiency compared to conventional approaches.

The growing demand for pilots due to the benefits of compact aircraft has been hindered by the challenges of their safe flight control. Successful automation can mitigate these issues by making these aircraft more manageable and comfortable to fly. Research into operator performance prediction in aviation has primarily focused on the tasks of tracking and smoothing the path of the vehicle. Our study expands on these findings by investigating the streamlined flight control of integrated systems with autonomous control. This research evaluates the effectiveness of different control strategies through the lens of flight quality, energy usage, and flight time. By understanding and addressing the limitations of current automated systems, this work contributes valuable knowledge to the field of integrated systems with application in various modes of transportation.

The Containerized application of Microservices has effectively addressed the scalability challenges of enterprise systems, yet System Admins face a pressing issue - determining container demand accurately. Over- and under-provisioning of containers leads to resource waste and performance issues. To address this gap, there's a need for an automated tool that predicts container demand based on future user needs, ultimately streamlining enterprise resource allocation. However, providing such cross-timeframe guarantees requires identifying application behaviors that change over time due to user activity patterns, ultimately requiring dynamic policy adjustment. Current user activity detection systems fail to consider system call timeouts that may skew results, despite being common in real-world scenarios. Additionally, the traditional approach of compiling static business rules may not account for scenarios that fall outside predefined parameters, whereas machine learning offers a flexible, parameter-driven alternative. Given the complexity of application behaviors and user patterns, the development of automated learning tools is crucial - particularly in scenarios involving frequent system interactions and communication delays.

Research into item-by-item algorithms like Modern Portfolio Theory and Dimensionality Reduction often focuses on their theoretical foundations. However, their practical applications are rarely validated against that of item-by-item approaches. We investigate the relationship between these models and linear models operating within the concept space. Our study begins with an examination of Susan Athey and Scott Voelker's work on comparing linear models with random models, and we expand upon it by comparing the performance of these models against one another. Through the use of the HOAK algorithm, we develop a concept space with ordered associations and assess the efficacy of linear models within such landscapes. Our research highlights the importance of the structure of associations among concepts for the performance of these models. To validate our findings against the practical challenges of working with matrices of ratings, we apply these models to datasets comprising Kickstarter project ratings. Our evaluation reveals that random models in the concept space outperform their distributed counterparts, and in many cases, they also perform better than classically used item-by-item algorithms.

Recent research has brought up the possibility that groups of young stars might be held in place by a massive black hole at the center of some galaxies. As more data becomes available from powerful telescopes, the number of potential cases is expected to grow, prompting the need for a reliable method to analyze the ages and movements of these stars. In response, we have updated our previous code, SAGE, which is capable of determining the age distribution of these stars and testing various models that might Spherical Mass Concentrations exist. Through an internal testing process, we have confirmed that our age determination method is capable of accurately recovering true age distributions and that our detection method for SMCs is unbiased. Through analysis of publicly available data, SAGE has been able to reproduce known results for the Central Arrangement of Stars in the Galaxy NGC 3516, but have found no evidence of a dense concentration of mass in the galaxies IC 1613, NGC 1068, NGC 3395, and NGC 3518. Furthermore, SAGE has been used to analyze a newly collected dataset, the Young Stars Near the Center of the Galaxy IC 3558, and has been able to recover previous age distribution findings, but has also revealed that there is no significant gradient in the velocities of these stars. Through our age distribution and velocity gradient analysis, SAGE has successfully classified a large dataset, the Stellar Mass Near Galaxies
The focus of this report is on demonstrating the effectiveness of using Random Model Predictive Control in the process of regulating a magnetic levitation system.

The increasing availability of online data necessitates the development of efficient methods for identifying patterns in digital information. However, traditional techniques such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA) become impractically slow and memory-consuming with massive datasets. This paper presents a two-phase approach to address this need: first, developing a theoretical framework linking compressed data from online streams with the computational results of PCA, and second, creating a component-based framework for implementing this theory in both memory and processing power-constrained environments. By achieving these goals, the proposed framework enables the development of scalable, memory-efficient, and time-efficient online methods for analyzing complex data.

A cellular automaton model, based on the principle of competition-colonization balance, was developed to investigate the dynamical processes of colonization and species extinction. This principle posits that competition between species can be resolved through a balance between a species' ability to defend defended territories against invasion and its ability to invade unoccupied territories. This study shows that the competition-colonization balance generates complex patterns of extinction, where one species eventually dominates, excluding all others. Moreover, we found that the competition can lead to long-term coexistence of multiple species, along with 1/f noise power spectra and fractal spatial distributions resembling those observed in real-world species distributions.

We establish a type of long-range order known as long-range order in a class of abelian quantum dual lattice models called primary models, which exhibit a pattern of ordering that arises from a specific, non-local relationship between orders and disorders. Building on a previously introduced method to define long-range order in quantum systems without a direct correspondence with an observable physical quantity, we determine the existence of this order through the convergence of a correlation function that measures the interaction between non-local currents. As a direct result, it is shown that a key parameter, the screening length associated with a specific local current, increases exponentially as the temperature approaches zero. Furthermore, we prove that the set of algebras associated with finite regions (algebra of type I) has a specific structure and is separated from the bulk algebra (type III) due to a significant difference in the correlations between currents extended to infinite lengths.

Our study investigates how entanglement is generated in a magnon-photon-phonon system through feedback connections. Specifically, we examine the entanglement between individual magnons and photons in a chamber magnometronic circuit that includes two magnons, one photon, and one phonon. We demonstrate that this entastanglement can be measured using the logarithmic negativity. Moreover, our findings reveal that coherent feedback connections play a significant role in enhancing and extending entanglement preservation. In particular, we evaluate three types of coherent feedback: cross-magnonic, cross-magnophononic, and cross-photon-magnonic feedback. According to our calculations, the entanglement between a magnon and a phonon via phononic feedback is superior to others, yet maintaining individual magnon-photon entanglement relies on cross-magnonic feedback. Furthermore, our study reveals that temperature adversely affects entanglement behavior, but coherent feedback helps mitigate this impact to some extent.

Closed expressions for one-loop triple-collinear splitting matrices in QCD have been derived and documented, applicable to all LO PDFs and a specific higher-order PDF. The triple-collinear regulators used serve as precursors to certain two- and one-collinear regulators. This approach offers an advantage by allowing higher-loop corrections to these regulators to be analytically resolved and confirms that no such corrections exist beyond one loop. Moreover, these splitting matrices incorporate complete finite virtual contributions, thereby eliminating any ambiguity in the redefinition of the higher-order PDFs or the treatment of massive particles in QCD. The underlying method involves a new quasi-distribution framework and is known to be versatile and generalizable to other theories.

A formal proof for the Neron Desingularization in one-dimensional local domains has been formulated and analyzed. This concept, initially introduced in EGA, finds an application in determining the Quotient Sheaf $\mathcal{E}xt^1(\Omega_{X/k}, P)$, which leads to a metric Frobenius study of non-smooth varieties in the context of Berthelot's arithmetic differential theory. This metric extension is more versatile and accommodates schemes of non-smooth varieties in arithmetic families with an underlying smooth structure.

The Indonesian Sundial Recording Application is a cross-platform mobile tool developed for capturing metadata of sundials in fieldwork. This app facilitates the creation of detailed archival information about sundials, enhancing research efficiency. As a comprehensive resource, the data collected through this application will support a wider range of studies on Java's Sundelikka cultural heritage.

This correspondence explores an emergent technology that integrates Data Delivery (D2D) within a unified framework, where an Intellect-Reflecting Surface aids in balancing D2D data transfer and power transmission. By reconfiguring electrical properties and reflecting signals with great precision, the Intellect-Reflecting Surface can optimize the end-to-end data rate and minimize power consumption at the D2D source. A two-phase algorithm with alternating minimization and low-complexity power distribution is proposed. Additionally, a successive convex approximation algorithm is developed to resolve non-convex subproblems efficiently.

The LIDAR-DV (Laser Induced Vaporization) technique utilizes a conventional laser and high-speed camera to obtain depth information. Researchers send a laser pulse, a camera captures the induced glow, analyzes the movement of particles within the captured frames. Obtaining a 2D depth map requires either a grid of lasers or specialized equipment, a grid of cameras, or complex reconstruction methods. In this study, a simpler approach was developed using conventional equipment to obtain 2D depth maps from a single camera and point laser. By inducing a laser-induced glow and capturing it from an angle, a depth profile can be obtained. Combining this profile with image rotation enables the generation of 2D depth maps. Our research demonstrated the feasibility of this technique on samples like paper and wood by comparing the obtained profiles with traditional methods.

In a directed graph, each vertex is assigned a set of edges, the number of which is equal to the vertex set's size, forming a linear map from edges to vertices. We examine a type of linear inequality involving the eigenvectors of the graph's adjacency matrix, which determines a convex body known as the first-order adjacency polytope. This paper focuses on the properties of this adjacency matrix in 1-transitive graphs with an automorphism group of primitive type, particularly those of almost simple nature. A notable result shows that for a specific, known family of symmetric graphs of rank 3, the second largest eigenvalue has multiplicity two and yields a unique, extreme point in the first-order adjacency spectrum with all positive entries in its corresponding eigenvector.

A novel phase disk with modifiable properties has been introduced to enhance the imaging capabilities of transmission electron microscopes. This phase disk can be reprogrammed using a personal computer through specialized hardware, incorporating magnetic coils made up of voxels that give rise to a quadratic wavefront transformation. By leveraging a digital control system, we are able to generate unique phase correction patterns, responsive to the electron beam's incoming wavefront distortions. By exploring the effects of multiple coil configurations on partial coherence scenarios, we observed the emergence of boron nitride's (h-BN) nanoscale defects, achieving an outstanding contrast in both incoherent and coherent modes, along with a remarkable 40\% enhancement in spatial resolution. Furthermore, our findings demonstrate the potential for real-time image optimization by adjusting the degree of coherence to the electron beam's spectral characteristics. Our research introduces an innovative approach to adaptive wavefront control and sheds light on the dynamic behavior of matter, paving the way for the realization of next-generation electron microscopes with dynamic phase discards.

A fundamental challenge in physics is how to quantify the effectiveness of theoretical models in describing real-world phenomena. In this discussion, we examine the link between the relative difference between prediction and observation, and the relative difference between the model's expectation value and its true value. To begin, a clear definition of 'calculation' is established, and relevant concepts from statistical inference are introduced. Ultimately, our goal is to establish a statistical framework for evaluating calculations.

The number of positions reachable from the origin after n steps on a d-dimensional integer grid is counted as a function of n, denoted as a(n,d), where each step moves in a coordinate direction by one unit. For a fixed dimension d, this sequence shows asymptotic behavior as n increases, which also displays oscillations related to the periodicity of the sequence and its relative size depending on the parity of d.

This research builds upon previous work by extending the Euclidean spacetime extension of Thorne-Gaskell's model to include R-R coordinates in the context of quantum gravity. We investigate how this expansion impacts the global structure and causal properties of the spacetime, discovering that the horizon disappears and is replaced by a global, non-singular geometry composed of multiple sheets connected by wormhole-like throats. Furthermore, our findings demonstrate that particles can traverse these connections, effectively moving between different universes within the spacetime. In addition, we calculate the quasinormal frequencies of this spacetime for varying quantum numbers, finding that they exhibit a distinct discrete, symmetric distribution around zero. Ultimately, these findings provide substantial evidence supporting the classical and quantum equivalence between the Thorne-Gaskell model and the Lemos-Fibber-Magana-Ponce model.

Our research explores how thermal energy affects heat shielding in graphene sheets modified with adatoms. By using the non-equilibrium Green's function over a static lattice approach, we've determined the system's thermal properties and found that the unique heat capacity of small, finite graphene sheets stems from atomic modifications within the graphene band structure. Furthermore, our study reveals that the distinct thermal behavior of these systems can be understood by examining phonon phonon interactions in graphene, along how the atomic modifications influence the carbon lattice's phonon phonon properties.

The MaskedSpeech model generates speech by masking portions of the audio signal and learning to reconstruct the masked sections along with the surrounding unmasked portions. Unlike traditional methods that generate speech step-by-step, MaskedSpeech operates on fixed-length audio segments and focuses solely on reconstructing the masked sections rather than the entire sequence. Our key innovations include employing a masking mechanism to encourage the model to leverage contextual information during training and a cross-species encoder-decoder architecture. Notably, the base MaskedSpeech model outperforms strongly supervised methods, such as WaveNet-based models, on a multiple speaker TTS system and demonstrates comparable performance to the Transformer-TTS and Demo-TTS methods in terms of speech quality.

This study presents two innovative concepts to streamline Bayesian predictive inference for large-scale machine learning models. Firstly, it introduces the idea of using latent variables to group similar input points together, reducing computational efficiency by focusing on a smaller set of representative points. This is applied to hidden space mapping, a technique that enhances SVM performance using variational inference. Secondly, it proposes to simplify the process by collapsing the multiple copies of these representative points into a single point, retaining uncertainty while eliminating redundancy. This approach can serve as a preprocessing step to speed up convergence in hidden space mapping. The research aims to boost the practical usage of variational Bayesian methods on larger datasets and address a related computational challenge.

Previous line-of-research has primarily concentrated on both conventional
machine learning models that rely on white box neural networks and more recent
adversarial attacks on large language models. However, there have been no prior
investigations into deceptive generative models generating high-performance,
robust attacks that target the limitations of the former and the latter.

Our work seeks to overcome the shortcomings of conventional adversarial attacks
by utilizing deceptive generative models to generate sophisticated and subtle
adversarial examples through an attack chain. We refer to the initial model in
the attack chain, which generates the input examples, as the black box and the
subsequent helper models, which refine the attacks, as the white boxes.

We have established that our proposed method yields the strongest generative
model-based attack against classification tasks for CNNs on the IMAGENET dataset
when assisted by white box models. Furthermore, our results demonstrate that
our proposed method successfully generates the most subtle generative model-based
attack against classification tasks for GPT-3, which would be difficult to
distinguish from the original input for a human.

Climate change misinformation is a pressing issue amplified by social media platforms. One particularly persistent myth hindering climate education is the claim that major institutions have synchronized their climate reports to artificially create a period of perceived climate stability. Contrary to this claim, our investigation reveals that such coordination has occurred historically among these institutions. However, our analysis of climate tweets related to this myth during periods of actual climate change and perceived climate stability finds that it contributes to climate misinformation regardless of the underlying climate conditions. This study aims to identify nuances within this common climate change misinformation, uncover the factual basis behind it, and promote climate literacy by encouraging users to discover and spread verified information on social media during any climate change indication.

Researchers have investigated the possibility of producing dark matter along with a single top quark or a pair of top quarks in proton-proton collisions at a 13 TeV energy level. To do this, simulations were performed using effective field theories and modified Smirnov-Owladuni type models, which involve interactions between dark matter, top quarks, and other particles. By analyzing data collected from the ATLAS and CMS experiments and comparing it to predictions from these models, researchers have placed limits on the parameters associated with these interactions. As a result, constraints have been imposed on the parameters of a dimension-5 and dimension-6 operator, with a cutoff scale of approximately 1150 GeV and 520 GeV respectively. Also, transverse momentum and decay width of the top quark have been calculated and their values found to be around 45 GeV and $10^{-3}$ respectively. Also, inverse decay width of the top quark has been calculated and found to be around $10^{-3}$.

In a n-exangulated framework of an abelian category, we establish two key theorems - one on non-exanglement and the other on 2-angled exact sequences. Building on these, we are able to prove the existence of a non-singular tilting n-exanglement structure, which subsequently enables the creation of a derived equivalence between a given n-exangulated category and its associated stable category following an tilting n-exanglement structure.

This paper provides a mathematical proof for the return to diversity in LATE estimation by demonstrating that the effect of instrument variability on LATE estimation precision depends on the balance between treatment options chosen by different subgroups defined by unobserved characteristics. In scenarios where individuals have access to multiple sources of information (disciplines), the variation in instrument return to diversity can be quantified and measured, given certain assumptions about discipline adoption patterns, regardless of the specific nature of those assumptions. Furthermore, the study examines the practical relevance of its findings by analyzing the relationship between university disciplines and voting behavior in Italy.

High-quality production of super J/psi for 40-50% branch ratio decay into electron positron pairs in electron-positron collisions is leveraged by PSI's electron accelerator facility, PEGASUS. Precise calibration ensures high-flux, low-background conditions during anisotropic decay accumulation. Consequently, numerous experiments examining less-studied J/psi decay channels involving, for instance, rare light meson interactions, neutron properties in various states, and fragmented baryons, are now feasible. Furthermore, applications of these capabilities to cutting-edge research in nuclear and particle physics and particle astrophysics are also discussed.

Planetary systems that form in a triple star arrangement face a common challenge: the short-lived presence of P-type disks that hinder the formation of planets at large distances from their host stars. Research has shown that the birth of the third star in these systems can significantly affect orbital mechanics, utilizing an asymmetrical gravitational force that shortens the formation time of planetary bodies. A new study aims to investigate this complex dynamic by employing N-body simulations to examine P-type triple star systems that form in a short period and analyze how they impact the length of orbits. By incorporating a simplified model that accounts for the gravitational influence of an accretion disk, researchers discovered that short-period binaries tend to see their orbit lengths shortened at a rate approximately ten times greater than those consisting of long-period binaries. This rate holds true regardless of other prevailing theories that suggest using nodal precession to explain this phenomenon. The rate is found to be influenced by two key variables, both directly proportional to one another: binary period and optical depth. This implies that binaries with higher optical depth experience a shorter time frame. An important application of these findings involves evaluating the potential habitability of planets residing in the habitable zone of short-period binaries with highly dense disks.

Our investigation has found that the conformal mode of the metric significantly influences lattice artifacts. As the lattice becomes increasingly fine, this effect diminishes. Utilizing a lattice with a fixed lattice spacing, we have discovered that lattice artifacts primarily contribute to a constant term in the cosmological evolution equation. This allows us to express the Hamiltonian constraint in the form characteristic of a de Sitter space. Furthermore, we have found that quantum corrections to the constraint influence the de Sitter curvature. In our model, we contrasted matter's back-reaction with that of the conformal mode. We observed that fluctuations in the conformal mode significantly decrease with lattice granularity. In the conformal matter model, we calculated the mass of fluctuations. We calculated the mass of fluctuations, finding it proportional to the lattice spacing's inverse. We have estimated the conformal mode quantum corrections to the constraint. We estimated that higher-order corrections likely constitute approximately 1% of the zero-order constraint when the lattice spacing corresponds to approximately 100 times the Hubble radius.

This paper presents a data-driven approach, addressing the diverse challenges in partitioning images based on various criteria. The proposed method unifies and reconciles disparate image segmentation models, including those developed by Chen et al. (2011), to facilitate a comprehensive framework. By integrating these models, we demonstrate their effectiveness in a range of applications and provide a mathematical foundation for predictive analysis. Our framework synergizes the principles of variational image partitioning with denoising, inpainting, and in coloring techniques, resulting in improved image segmentation and color restoration. Our results show that the proposed method outperforms existing image segmentation methods, as well as deep learning-based approaches in terms of denoising, inpainting, and image color restoration.

Heavy spinning objects interacting with certain very light fields can cause energy transfer that increases the spinning object's rotation, countering the expected decline in its spin over time. This phenomenon—called superradiance instability—provides a mechanism that could have established the properties of neutrinos and other bosonic fields as observed today. Researchers have used the correlation between the quasar J1401+2128 and its companion the quasar cluster SDSS J1146+292 while they were undergoing the instability to improve the known range of boson masses. Further enhancement of this research is possible if in the future gravitational waves can be detected from early black holes. Developing this research direction may provide insight that in the end boson instability may have set its properties as seen today.

The human brain's ability to solve complex problems has long inspired computer architecture and electronic circuit design. Over the past decade, neuro-morphic chip design has gained increased attention. The recently released Apple M1 chip, containing an 8core Havellis, highlights the significant potential of neuro-morphic computing in high-performance applications. To test and optimize algorithms on neuro-morphic architectures, sophisticated software tools are required. Currently, limited software support hinders full development of neuro-morphic computing applications. To address this, we developed an "in-the-software" approach, utilizing Brian to emulate Loihi's neuro-morphic capabilities. Our approach enables efficient exploration of neuro-morphic algorithm design without specialized hardware. A comparison of different data mapping methods on Loihi, emulated with Brian, revealed that partitioning memristive crossbar arrays and balancing data distribution are critical factors for optimizing neuro-morphic performance. The simulation also demonstrated the superiority of spiking neurons over threshold neurons in most cases, while identifying scenarios where threshold neurons excel. The simulation exposed a trade-off between neuromorphic and traditional digital computing, showing that neuro-morphic designs are particularly advantageous for spiking neurons due to their increased computational load per non-linear operation. The research deepens our understanding of neuro-morphic computing and provides valuable insights into developing and optimizing algorithms for neuro-morphic systems. The approach supports the exploration of novel algorithms and offers the advantage of rapid testing and iteration.

This study  examines the physical properties of a noise storm  that occurred above a X-class flare using multi-frequency radio spectroscopy 
and multi-wavelength imagery from the STEREO, SDO, RHESSI and NuSTAR satellites. 
A microflare detected by STEREO/Bellatrix prior to the peak of the main flare 
exhibits a distinct narrow burst in NuSTAR data, suggesting that an organized 
plasma ejection preceded the flare emission. 
Additionally, two radio sources evolving in parallel were found in TESS imagery 
during the microflare and peak flare events, respectively. 
Multiple signs pointing to non-thermal electrons were discovered for these sources. 
Initial findings suggest a field line connection responsible for both a minor 
rearrangement in STEREO projections and an observed change in magnetic twist. 
Following this, the main flare causes the merging of these sources near the 
X2 region, suggesting a significant loss of magnetic stability due to the 
peak microflare-induced release of stored energy. 
This study provides another example of loss of magnetic stability caused by 
radio bursts resulting from both inductive and bremsstrahlung emissions against 
the background of a major solar flare.

Researchers have developed an innovative method to integrate the creation of an optical magnetron and an optically trapped particle into a single 2D plane. By combining these techniques, they enable simultaneous measurement of the optical magnetron's behavior and the rotational dynamics of the trapped particle. Using a lightweight polystyrene bead as a test subject, they demonstrated the effectiveness of this approach by observing the complex interaction of the trapped bead with a rotating magnetic field, including its response to opposing forces. Furthermore, the research shows that this technique offers a versatile platform for investigating the dynamics and properties of fine particles, potentially aiding in the study of spinning particles and the study of biomolecules.

Investigating how a cluster of particles influences accretion onto a non-rotating black hole, where particles are held in orbit by their mutual interactions.  Where a theory predicting accretion rates based on specific angular momentum is explored, which shows rates increase with M^5/3 for low momentum and stable matter distributions, and decrease with density for high momentum, following l^5/(rho tl)^2 formulae.  It's observed that any stable arrangement of particles has these properties, and so it seems reasonable to assume the same trend applies to unstable arrangements.  Given this, it's proposed that the rate at which a sphere of particles decreases in mass is proportional to its L5/2 ratio.

A key point is raised concerning an atom in motion near a flat, narrow surface that is crucial for interpreting data on electromagnetic signals generated by moving atoms near mesoscopic particles. It's discovered and demonstrated analytically that when this atom moves parallel to a dielectric surface, its levels become coupled and resonance frequencies shift due to the motion. Additionally, new unknown emitters appear and absorb energy from the atom's excitation, in addition to the well-known "anti-atom" and "point" radiating mechanisms. This study shows that the mechanisms generating electromagnetic emissions can be understood and predicted based on the direction and speed of the atom's motion.

Recent discoveries of "blue giant" stars beyond the core of young star cluster Westerlund 2 have prompted a detailed analysis of its outskirts using Gaia DR2 data. This study identifies blue giants matching the characteristics of single-star evolution, noting that many such stars exhibit evolved properties. However, some exhibited evidence of binarity at close ranges but lack evidence at further distances. Furthermore, checks into cluster members beyond the core reveal no significant findings. These results indicate that the majority of Westerlund 2's blue giants are not associated with this cluster and likely stem from single-star evolution, possibly involving the Haumea pathway. Conversely, analysis of cluster and its core stars using the fixed magnitude method shows an inconsistency in mass loss rates. This discrepancy could be explained by considering mass loss rates that account for both upper mass limits and stochastic events.

This study investigates a minimal energy problem in the $H^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ space for a given parameter $\mu > 0$. The standard ground state solution to this problem is demonstrated to exist. In addition, we examine the asymptotic behavior of this solution. To support our findings, we provide a numerical example validating our theoretical findings.

Historical documents and exam papers often suffer from age-related degradation, yellowing, and browning, which can also be exacerbated by ink smearing, smudging, and blurring. These factors complicate the initial stages of document analysis and image enhancement techniques have been proposed to mitigate such degradation and enhance overall document quality. Nevertheless, current approaches mainly focus on color correction and color constancy but neglect other critical elements. In contrast, our method employs a multi-task adversarial network framework that prioritizes image sharpness over color correction. Our novel network architecture integrates a spatial frequency-based adversarial network and a multi-scale generator network to improve degraded document images. Our results on the IAPR 2011 2D Image Super-Resolution challenge demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in enhancing handwritten document image quality. Additionally, our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art image enhancement techniques on multiple public datasets.

The reliance on paper documentation is gradually waning as people prefer digital formats due to ease of management and storage. Unfortunately, existing digital formats do not fully meet these needs, leading to a continued requirement for paper files that can be scanned and later processed. Unfortunately, the proliferation of electronic data hinders processing and management. To address this problem, a novel method for extracting data from ID documents has been proposed, combining recognized technologies such as keyphrase extraction, part-of-speech tagging, and noun phrase identification. The proposed method uses 2D and 1D optical character recognition to convert ID documents into text and subsequently employs a machine-learned model to categorize the content of the ID documents and extract relevant information. The proposed method has been tested on a dataset of 1310 images and yielded accurate results for different ID fields, with accuracy rates of 96.03% for name, 98.32% for parent's name, 97.94% for issue date, 97.56% for expiration date, and 98.17% for ID number. The extraction process is facilitated by the ETL library, developed in-house to streamline data extraction and loading.

A practical, real-time channel assessment method is crucial for developing adaptive systems in unlicensed IEEE 802.11p standard network communications. The goal of this study is to enhance the performance of IEEE 802.11p channel estimation using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), incorporating an adaptive learning rate and a pre-trained model, through data from the MAC layer. To address the issue of insufficient training data, a complex data enhancement technique based on linear convolution is implemented to create a comprehensive and diverse training set. The proposed method is then verified by temporarily averaging the output of the training and validation sets to evaluate its accuracy across different IEEE 802.11p subcarriers, frequencies, and packet lengths. By eliminating hyperparameter tuning and hyperparameter-driven errors, our proposed method offers a robust alternative. Compared to conventional IEEE 802.11p channel estimation, our method demonstrates a 10-20 dB improvement in SNR and reduces bit error rate accordingly.

The properties of plasma in the celestial realm can be inferred by In-Situ measurements taken directly from it. The variations of plasma parameters influence the color of the captured images, and knowing this color can provide a preliminary understanding of the local environment, particularly its large-scale and high-level characteristics. In this research, a novel approach is proposed to determine the properties of plasma through analysis of image data captured by celestial cameras using a network of transport based on generative adversarial methods. The plasma transport model incorporates plasma's essential characteristics, and a detailed assessment of its functionality reveals that it is capable of reconstructing key plasma parameters such as electron density temperature, particle velocity, and magnetic field strength. The selection of these characteristics greatly affects the performance of the model; choosing inappropriate parameters leads to unwanted artifacts in the training process. Furthermore, careful consideration of the model's architecture and the number of cells within it plays a crucial role in ensuring accurate plasma parameter reconstruction. Consideration of these factors enables development of a reliable and efficient algorithm for analyzing celestial plasma's electronic density, temperature, and other essential properties. The research highlights a novel approach to analyzing celestial images through application of machine learning techniques, and Nishchal et al. highlight various challenges associated with this approach.

We present a novel neural network design that utilizes the universal approximation property of ReLU activation functions. Given data points from a d-dimensional space and corresponding labels, our method first determines an n_b node count in the hidden layer by solving a system of inequlities via linear programming. Next, it calculates the optimal vector coordinates for these n_b nodes in a given dimension p_v, also through linear programming. This dimension p_v should be at least d+1 to ensure hidden layer stability. Although our algorithm has N^2 node complexity in both node count and optimization complexity, making it computationally costly, we have developed more efficient variations by reducing constraints in each stage. These reduced complexity algorithms may place hidden layer nodes in a lower dimensional space at the cost of suboptimal node counts. While this trade-off potentially harms performance in terms of node count, we found that a smaller node count often correlates with better performance due to overfitting issues. Overall, our study presents two key advantages. First, we provide simple geometric criteria for estimating node counts in the neural network, facilitating automatic node count selection. Second, we demonstrate that support vector machine methods can be effectively replaced by universal approximation property in determining node positions. These two features can be also applied to other types of neural networks.

This paper introduces the ECFA Early Career Researcher's Committee: its origins,
composition, operational guidelines, and recent achievements during the 2021-2022 period.

A material with different properties at two different frequency ranges creates a boundary that can guide the waves of those frequencies along its surface. These guided waves leverage quantum-like interactions between the waves within one range and their counterparts in the second range, enhancing their likelihood of existence. Researchers have previously utilized this phenomenon across various fields, such as sound waves in two distinct media and light in a contrasting material arrangement. In this study, the concept is applied to developing devices that control multiple frequencies of light, such as those produced by different lasers, by carefully designing a boundary with two distinct materials. The results indicate that such a boundary can effectively guide these lasers and may be utilized to increase the efficiency of devices like lasers themselves.

In the long-term goal of creating intelligent systems like the embodied cognitive AI embodied in a robot like NAO that learn through multi-agent collaboration with humans and robots, significant hurdles remain to be overcome in terms of modeling numerous cooperative learning interactions to generate vast amounts of data.  To overcome this challenge, this research aims to develop a transparent cognitive AI framework that enables large-scale multi-agent cooperative learning to take place.  By designing a fully automated data management system, including data collection, storage, processing, and analysis, the research seeks to efficiently manage and optimize learning data within an extensive multi-agent cooperative learning environment, thus maximizing data-driven model performance improvements.  Key to this cognitive AI system is an advanced data processing engine capable of real-time data manipulation utilizing multi-threading techniques to maintain high throughput and dependability under heavy load conditions.  Within an empirical evaluation of this cognitive AI system, a cooperative learning dataset was successfully compiled, processed utilizing the data processing engine and analyzed using advanced statistical methods.  This research contributes to the development of an efficient and manageable framework for large-scale multi-agent cooperative learning environments to maximize performance improvements through data-driven approaches.

In robust statistical analysis, the median absolute deviation (MAD) offers an advantage
over standard measures of dispersion, such as being less influenced by outliers.
However, standard MAD estimates can still be biased, particularly in cases with small
data sets. This document proposes two alternative estimation methods for the MAD
that reduce its bias. These new estimators maintain its robust properties, and under
normal distribution conditions, they perform similarly to biased and bias-reduced
versions of standard variance estimators, such as the sample variance and minimum
variance unbiased estimator (UMVUE). Finally, the document evaluates the proposed
estimators through simulation studies and provides recommendations based on those
results.

Recent breakthroughs in open-domain question answering have primarily relied on knowledge graph augmentation through relational extraction from text. Although this method has produced satisfactory results for diverse query types, it has a significant limitation in that it necessitates a substantial amount of labeled data and computing resources. To circumvent this constraint, we propose a novel method of integrating knowledge graphs that focuses on predicting missing relationships within an incomplete graph structure. Our approach utilizes this prediction to improve the knowledge graph augmentation process for a given query, thereby enabling the inclusion of previously unconsidered实体 pairs. As a result, this increase in the number of实体 pairs available as answers leads to enhanced performance in terms of accuracy. Our proposed method has yielded remarkable results, with a 1.29-point improvement in F1-score and 0.97-point boost in exact match scores on the TREC 2019 common test set.
